name: Panner Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Panner Disease

criteria.description: History of elbow pain and limited range of motion, especially in young children
Radiographic evidence of irregularity, fragmentation, and sclerosis of the capitellum
Onset typically between 5 and 15 years of age
Exclusion of other causes of elbow pain such as osteochondritis dissecans

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical symptoms consistent with elbow pain and limited motion plus radiographic findings characteristic of capitellar osteochondrosis, with exclusion of other diagnoses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; MRI may be used for further evaluation.

occasional.symptomName: Abnormality of blood and blood-forming tissues
Irregular articular surfaces of the elbow joints

laboratory: Normal inflammatory markers; no specific laboratory abnormalities
imaging: X-ray showing irregularity, fragmentation, and sclerosis of the capitellum epiphysis
MRI demonstrating edema and fragmentation of the capitellar ossification center
other: History of repetitive microtrauma or overuse in young athletes

distinguishingFeatures: Typically affects older children and adolescents
Presence of loose bodies in the joint
More severe cartilage involvement on imaging
Systemic symptoms such as fever and rash

redFlags: Persistent severe elbow pain unresponsive to conservative treatment
Progressive loss of elbow range of motion
Signs of joint infection or systemic illness
references: Panner Disease: Clinical and Radiographic Features. Journal of Pediatric Orthopedics, 2018.
Orphanet Report on Panner Disease, ORPHA:97336.
Imaging of Pediatric Elbow Disorders. Radiographics, 2020.
